title: Brioche half-pi shawl
subtitle: A DK semicircle in two-colour brioche, using Elizabeth Zimmermann's half-pi shaping.
excerpt: A DK semicircular shawl using Elizabeth Zimmermann's half-pi construction with a body worked entirely in two-colour brioche stitch. The logarithmic increase schedule naturally pairs with the brioche doubling rows. Wingspan approximately 150 cm, centre-back depth approximately 58 cm. About 250 g each of two DK yarns in contrasting values.
sourceNotes: The half-pi construction is Elizabeth Zimmermann's invention (Knitting Without Tears, 1971). Two-colour brioche technique is documented in Nancy Marchant, Brioche Knitting (2010). Combining the half-pi construction with two-colour brioche is an original synthesis; Marchant's book covers semicircle brioche shawls but not specifically the half-pi schedule.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts × 36 rows = 10 × 10 cm in two-colour brioche on 4.5 mm needles, relaxed.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 150 cm. Centre-back depth approximately 58 cm. Relaxed (not blocked).

glossaryTerms.definition: Elizabeth Zimmermann's logarithmic semicircle shaping: stitch count doubles on increase rows spaced at 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, and 36 plain rows between increase rows.

A row in which every stitch is replaced by a k1, yo — effectively doubling the stitch count on the needle. In brioche construction the doubling row starts a new brioche section after the half-pi increase.
Knit the next stitch together with its paired yarn-over from the previous row. In two-colour brioche this is worked with the colour not used on the previous pass.

content.text: A DK semicircular shawl using Elizabeth Zimmermann's
half-pi construction
with two-colour brioche throughout. Between the doubling increase rows, the half-pi plain rows are worked as two-colour brioche passes. A
brioche doubling row
replaces each half-pi increase row, simultaneously doubling stitch count and setting up the brioche pairs. Wingspan approximately 150 cm.

ADVANCED for two reasons: the two-colour brioche colour management, and the brioche doubling row technique which requires a deliberate set-up pass. The fabric is not wet-blocked. Budget about 250 g (about 550 m / 600 yards) of each of two DK yarns in contrasting values.

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over two-colour brioche on 4.5 mm needles, relaxed. Do not wet-block the gauge swatch: the relaxed swatch dimension is what counts. At gauge the 150 cm wingspan requires approximately 300 stitches at the cast-off row; working backwards through the half-pi schedule gives approximately 9 to 12 stitches as the starting count for section 1.
Stitches used

items.name: brk
items.qty: brioche knit: k stitch + its paired yo together

content.text: Pattern
Cast on
Using colour A and long-tail cast-on, cast on 9 stitches. Work 3 rows of plain garter in colour A to establish the straight top edge.
Half-pi schedule overview

Section 1: 3 brioche passes, then doubling row → 18 sts. Section 2: 6 passes, then doubling row → 36 sts. Section 3: 9 passes, then doubling row → 72 sts. Section 4: 18 passes, then doubling row → 144 sts. Section 5: 27 passes, then final plain passes → cast off at approximately 300 sts.
Standard brioche pass (between doubling rows)
Pass 1 (colour B, RS): sl1yo, *
brk
, sl1yo; repeat from * to last st, brk.
Pass 2 (colour A, WS): brk, *sl1yo, brk; repeat from * to end.
These 2 passes together = 1 brioche pair. Count pairs, not individual passes, against the half-pi schedule.
Brioche doubling row

Work the doubling row in colour A: *k1, yo; repeat from * to end. Stitch count doubles. Work the return pass in colour B as a set-up pass: sl1yo, *brk, sl1yo; repeat from *. The brioche pairs are now re-established on the doubled stitch count. Continue standard brioche passes.
Bind off
Work standard brioche bind-off in colour A: treat each brk as k, each sl1yo as k2tog before binding off. Work very loosely.
Common faults

Brioche pairs misaligned after the doubling row: the set-up pass was not worked before returning to the standard brioche pair. Without the set-up pass, the brk stitches have no paired yo to work into. Always work the colour B set-up pass immediately after the doubling row.

Wrong depth reached at the bind-off: the brioche pairs were counted as 1 pass instead of 2. Each half-pi section specifies brioche pairs, not individual passes. Section 4, for example, requires 18 full pairs = 36 individual passes before the doubling row.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water. Roll in a dry towel; lay flat to dry. Do not pin or stretch the brioche fabric.
What to try next

Work sections 1 to 3 in plain garter in one colour, then transition to two-colour brioche for sections 4 and 5. This gives a simpler gradient from plain garter at the spine to rich brioche at the lower edge.
